measurement: Per-task wall-clock cost of node/web coder tasks on a real 9-unit operator dispatch, and the measured effect of the #1337 file-tool guidance fix on consecutive tasks of that same run

hardware.gpu: Intel Arc 140V (Xe2) - coder model served by OpenVINO Model Server on :8000
hardware.npu: present, not used by this stage

toolchain.assistant_model: Qwen3-14B INT4 on GPU (swapped out while the coder runs)

subject.origin: operator-initiated `/dispatch advanced new pottery-studio | <goal>` from the BlarAI desktop app - NOT a battery card
subject.goal: a 4-page pottery studio website: home, pieces list, per-piece page, contact form
subject.stack: node / JavaScript (language-pinned so the acceptance oracle grades what was built)

methodology: Wall clock taken from the fleet journal's TASK-START/TASK-END pairs, which bracket the whole per-task cycle: decomposition handoff, candidate builds, gates, merge, and the post-merge visual-critique loop. n=1 per task; no task was repeated. The box was otherwise idle except for this session's own tooling. The #1337 guidance fix was applied to the LIVE AGENTS.md between task 1 and task 2, mid-run - so tasks 1 and 2+ differ in that one variable AND in their visual-fix counts, which is the confound named below.

results.note: Ran under the PRE-fix AGENTS.md. Every read/write/edit in the fix1 attempt was refused (0 OK / 8 denied) because the coder emitted leading-slash paths; it burned 40 steps and ~17 minutes routing around them with cat/cp/echo before self-correcting to drive-qualified paths. 3 visual-fix cycles.
First task under the corrected AGENTS.md. Every filePath emitted was fully drive-qualified.

Coder mid-stream at 13:55:59 (step 15, 3 edits); OVMS still serving that request at 13:56:29; assistant swapped back 13:56:36; all driving processes then exited. coord_redispatch staged a redispatch proposal at 14:02:35 which nothing consumes (#1321). The run ended here - the remaining 5 planned tasks were never dispatched.

cost_reading.prior_estimate_range_minutes: 40-85 (B3's first campaign run, the figure B9's budget was extrapolated from)
cost_reading.margin_note: 9 units at the post-fix rate is ~7.8 h against an 8 h budget. The extrapolated budget is roughly right and has almost NO margin: one task needing a second dispatch attempt (max_task_dispatches=4) exhausts it.

not_measured: MODEL time vs HARNESS overhead - #1322 DECISION 4's actual ask. These are end-to-end wall-clock figures only; the split needs instrumentation that does not exist.

Whether the 15.5-minute improvement is attributable to the #1337 fix ALONE. The denial count (11 -> 0) is exact and directly attributable; the minutes are confounded because task 1 also ran 3 visual-fix cycles and n=1 per arm. Do not quote the 23% as a clean causal figure.
GPU utilisation, power draw and thermals across the run.
Why contact-page parked. The coder was mid-request when OVMS stopped; whether that was a swap-back race, a resource event, or a coder failure is not established here.
Any figure for the 5 tasks that never dispatched - the run's total cost for a COMPLETE 9-unit product remains unmeasured.

This is NOT the B9 battery card. Same shape (4 pages, shared layout, one data source, contact form) on the same stack, but a different instrument. Treat as a strong prior for B9's per-unit cost, not as B9's measurement - B9 has still never completed a run.
